name: Typewolf
tagline: Site of the Day archive that names the typefaces on every site it features
description: Typewolf is Jeremiah Shoaf's independent typography resource: a daily Site of the Day gallery where every entry lists the exact typefaces the site uses, cross-linked to a page per font. It carries 1,140 font pages, 396 archive pages of featured sites, ranked font lists (Top 40 Google Fonts, Helvetica and Futura alternatives, top monospaced and slab serifs), lookbooks, and a free-fonts guide. The paid Flawless Typography Checklist is a 100-item interactive course at $399. It is the reference designers use to answer "what font is that site using" and to pick a pairing.
pricing_detail: Site is free. Flawless Typography Checklist is $399 USD one-time, lifetime access, 100 items across 6 sections plus a 180-typeface pairing cheatsheet.
agent_guidance: Reach for Typewolf when you need a real typeface pairing that shipped on a real site, not a generated palette of fonts. Every page is plain server-rendered HTML with no JS gate, so you can fetch a font page (typewolf.com/<font-slug>) or a list page (top-10-sans-serif-fonts, google-fonts) and read it directly — this is one of the few type resources an agent can actually parse. Watch out: robots.txt disallows /all-sites and /go/, most named fonts are commercial licences you cannot ship, and the Site of the Day feed has not been updated since Dec 14 2025, so treat it as an archive rather than a live trend feed.
why_it_matters: It is the only large public dataset that maps real websites to the exact typefaces they use, which makes it the best source for a pairing decision that has already survived contact with production. The font lists are opinionated and specific enough to act on.
notable_for: 396 archive pages of Site of the Day
evidence: https://typewolf.com (homepage), https://www.typewolf.com/site-of-the-day (Page 1 of 396), https://www.typewolf.com/all-fonts (states 1140 fonts), https://www.typewolf.com/checklist ($399, 100 items), https://www.typewolf.com/sitemap.xml (1,247 URLs), https://www.typewolf.com/robots.txt

name: Klim Type Foundry
tagline: New Zealand retail foundry behind Söhne, Tiempos, Founders Grotesk and Untitled Sans
description: Klim Type Foundry is Kris Sowersby's retail foundry, operating since 2005, with 55 published typeface pages grouped into 16 superfamilies plus 10 named custom commissions (PayPal Sans, Metric FC and others). It sells metered licences — desktop by seat, web by page views, app by monthly active users, OEM by device, advertising by impressions, broadcast by budget — with unlimited and enterprise tiers by quote. Free test fonts are available for internal evaluation only. Its in-use gallery holds over 1,400 documented uses.
pricing_detail: No flat price list. Desktop priced by number of users, web by page views or unique users, app by MAUs or total downloads, OEM by number of devices, advertising by monthly impressions, broadcast by production budget or audience size. Unlimited Web, Unlimited App and Enterprise are bespoke. Test fonts are free but restricted to internal use.
agent_guidance: Use Klim as the reference point when a brief calls for a serious paid workhorse — Söhne for UI sans, Tiempos for editorial serif, Untitled for a neutral default — but never put a Klim font into a build without the client's licence, because every family is a metered EULA and there is no free-for-commercial tier. Marketing and licence pages are plain HTML and readable, but the per-family buy pages render prices through JavaScript and return only "Loading, please wait…" to a fetcher, so quote licence structure, not numbers. Their robots.txt disallows GPTBot outright; if you need a substitute you can actually ship, fall back to Velvetyne or Uncut in this index.
why_it_matters: Klim's Söhne and Founders Grotesk defined the look of a whole decade of startup and editorial design, which makes it the honest benchmark against which any free alternative gets judged. Its published licence taxonomy is also the clearest explanation of how modern font metering works.
notable_for: Söhne, Tiempos, Founders Grotesk, Untitled Sans
free test fonts for internal evaluation
evidence: https://klim.co.nz (homepage, 34 families + 10 custom projects named), https://klim.co.nz/sitemap/sitemap-0.xml (1,668 URLs: 55 /fonts/ pages, 16 /collections/, 10 /custom-fonts/, 1,472 /in-use/), https://klim.co.nz/licences/, https://klim.co.nz/buy/soehne/ (prices JS-gated), https://klim.co.nz/robots.txt (GPTBot disallowed)

name: Pangram Pangram
tagline: 62 trend-forward families with free trial versions and commercial licences from $40
description: Pangram Pangram is a Montreal-based foundry selling 62 typeface families (198 individual products once sub-families are counted), including Neue Montreal, Monument, Editorial New, Right Grotesk and Telegraf. Every family has a free trial version you can download before buying, and commercial licences start at $40, which is unusually cheap for retail type. The storefront runs on Shopify, so the catalogue is available as JSON, and the site publishes an llms.txt and an agents.md for AI shopping agents.
pricing_detail: Commercial licences start at $40. Free trial version of every family. Font Starter Pack bundle and an Early Access tier are sold separately.
agent_guidance: This is the paid foundry an agent can actually work with: hit https://pangrampangram.com/products.json?limit=250 for the full 198-product catalogue as structured JSON, and read /llms.txt before scripting anything — it explicitly directs agents to the Shop skill instead of scraping the storefront. Prefer it over Klim when the budget is small and the brief wants a current geometric or neo-grotesque look; prefer Klim when the brand needs a typeface that will not date. Trial fonts are for comps only, so never ship a trial file in a production build.
why_it_matters: It is the rare commercial foundry that publishes machine-readable catalogue data and explicit agent instructions, which makes it the only paid type source in this index an automated workflow can query. The $40 entry price also puts real retail type inside a side-project budget.
notable_for: free trial version of every font
evidence: https://pangrampangram.com (homepage, "Showing 12 of 62 fonts"), https://pangrampangram.com/collections.json (All fonts = 62, All Families and Sub-Families = 198), https://pangrampangram.com/products.json?limit=250 (199 records), https://pangrampangram.com/sitemap.xml, https://pangrampangram.com/sitemap_agentic_discovery.xml, https://pangrampangram.com/llms.txt

name: Future Fonts
tagline: Marketplace for in-progress typefaces: buy at v0.1 cheap, get every later version free
description: Future Fonts sells typefaces that are still being drawn. A designer releases a workable v0.1, the price rises with each version, and anyone who bought early receives every later update at no extra cost. It carries roughly 367 typefaces from about 141 independent designers and foundries, including OH no Type Co, XYZ Type, Vectro and Nova. It was started in February 2018 by Lizy Gershenzon and Travis Kochel of Scribble Tone, and each designer sets their own prices and licence terms.
pricing_detail: No fixed price list. Each designer sets the price, which increases with every released version; early buyers keep the lower price and receive all future versions free.
agent_guidance: Send a human here, not a fetcher: futurefonts.xyz 301s to www.futurefonts.com and the site is a Vite single-page app whose raw HTML contains nothing but the title tag, so scraping returns an empty shell. The only machine-readable surface is the sitemap at s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/incremental-production/sitemap/sitemap.xml.gz, which yields the /<foundry>/<font> URL for all 367 typefaces. Use it when a brief wants a weird display face nobody else has shipped; use Pangram Pangram or Velvetyne instead when you need the actual font files inside an automated build.
why_it_matters: It changed how independent type gets funded by letting designers sell drafts and iterate with paying users, which is why so much genuinely new display type appears here first. Nothing else in the index gives you access to typefaces before they are finished.
notable_for: free updates forever for early buyers
evidence: https://futurefonts.xyz (301 to https://www.futurefonts.com/), https://www.futurefonts.com/ (JS shell, body text is just the title), https://www.futurefonts.com/robots.txt, sitemap at s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/incremental-production/sitemap/sitemap.xml.gz (518 URLs: 367 font pages, 141 distinct foundry paths), https://medium.com/future-fonts/introducing-futurefonts-xyz-8c0569777db6 (version model and founders)

name: Velvetyne Type Foundry
tagline: 42 libre typefaces under the SIL Open Font License, free for commercial use
description: Velvetyne is a French non-profit collective that designs and releases libre, open-source typefaces under the SIL Open Font License. Its catalogue holds 42 families — among them Karrik, Le Murmure, VG5000, Compagnon, Basteleur, Terminal Grotesque and Sligoil — all downloadable free and free to use commercially, with sources on GitLab. The collective also runs typography workshops and takes custom commissions, and is funded by donations rather than sales.
agent_guidance: This is the safest source in the typography set for anything you will actually ship: OFL means you can bundle, self-host and subset the files without a licence conversation, which Klim, Pangram Pangram and Future Fonts all forbid. Reach for it when a brief wants character rather than neutrality — Karrik and Le Murmure carry a brand, but none of these are Inter-grade UI workhorses, so pair them as display faces over a neutral system stack. Note that velvetyne.fr/robots.txt blocks several hundred AI user agents by name while granting ClaudeBot a crawl-delay, so throttle hard, and pull the font binaries from gitlab.com/velvetyne rather than hammering the site (the /fonts/ index page alone is 8.5 MB).
why_it_matters: It proves that genuinely experimental type can be released under a free licence, and it is the standard place designers go when a project needs personality without a font budget. Le Murmure and Karrik in particular now appear on commercial work that could have afforded retail type.
notable_for: 42 families, all SIL Open Font License
evidence: https://velvetyne.fr (homepage, 41 names listed), https://velvetyne.fr/fonts/ (42 distinct /fonts/<slug>/ links), https://velvetyne.fr/about/ (confirms SIL OFL, non-profit, GitLab, donations), https://velvetyne.fr/robots.txt (blocks ~500 AI user agents, ClaudeBot allowed with crawl-delay 1)

name: UNCUT.wtf
tagline: Curated catalogue of ~163 free and open-source contemporary typefaces
description: UNCUT.wtf is a curated catalogue of free and open-source typefaces made by Danish designer Kasper Nordkvist, launched in April 2021. Secondary sources put the collection at roughly 163 typefaces sorted into four classes — sans serif, serif, monospace and display — each with a direct link to the designer's own download. It aggregates rather than hosts, so the licence travels with each individual font and is not uniform across the catalogue. Note that the site now sits behind a proof-of-work bot check and could not be read directly during this pass.
agent_guidance: Do not try to fetch this one — uncut.wtf returns 403 to a normal fetcher and 454 with a Simply.com SHA-256 proof-of-work JavaScript challenge to a browser-agent string, so an agent gets a challenge page and nothing else. Treat it as a bookmark you hand to a human for browsing, and use Velvetyne or Google Fonts when you need font files a script can download. If you do get a font name out of it, verify that specific font's licence at its own source before shipping, because 'free' here covers everything from OFL to plain freeware with terms attached.
why_it_matters: It is the best-curated single view of contemporary free type — the place designers find the display face that does not look like a Google Fonts default. Its value is entirely editorial taste, which is also why it is worth nothing to an automated pipeline that cannot open it.
notable_for: links out to each designer's download
evidence: https://uncut.wtf (WebFetch: HTTP 403; curl with a Chrome user agent: HTTP 454 Simply.com proof-of-work challenge page, retried on www. with the same result). Counts and taxonomy are second-hand, from web search results and https://toolfolio.com/tools/uncut-wtf — not verified on the site itself.
